messages:
maria: kicking off canary deploy for router service v2 -> 10% traffic, config change to route prefix handling. deploying with deploy-bot now. watching latency, 95p and error rates closely.

deploy-bot: deploy started: router/v2 -> canary 10% (maria). rollout id=rl_20260315_01. CI checks passed.

maria: copying checks here — the change is small but touches prefix logic in request normalization. should be safe but tagging oncall. @jake you're oncall for releases today — FYI.

incident-bot: ALERT: router-service SLO burn detected. severity=P2. metric=latency_p95, window=5m, value=+18% vs baseline. paging: @jake @sasha

jake: i'm on it. looking at traces. can someone drop the current span link?

maria: span link: https://tracing.prod/redwood/router?trace=abc123 — seeing increased downstream waits to kv-cache.

jake: hmm. dashboards are... not showing per-route latency. we only have cluster-level p95. that's not helpful. looks like observability gap — i can't slice by prefix.

sasha: ugh we removed the per-route dashboard during the metrics rename last month. we promised to restore it in the observability sprint. bad timing.

jake: ok timeline: latency spike started ~2m after rollout. errors also ticked but not huge. i'll try to toggle the feature flag to stop the new routing for the canary. how to toggle?

maria: use feature-flag CLI: `ffctl set router_v2_canary false --env=prod --scope=canary`

jake: running now — `ffctl set router_v2_canary false --env=prod --scope=canary --reason="latency spike during canary"`

sre-bot: Feature flag update recorded. ff=router_v2_canary, value=false, actor=jake, scope=canary, id=ffop_7789.

incident-bot: Noted: killing canary flag. continuing to monitor metrics.

jake: after flip: p95 is dropping, error rate normalizing. still need to confirm rollback of rollout. maria can you trigger rollback of the canary?

maria: rolling back rollout id=rl_20260315_01 -> rollback started via deploy-bot. command: `deploy-bot rollback rl_20260315_01 --confirm`

deploy-bot: rollback initiated. target state: pre-deploy. expected 2-3min for traffic stabilization.

jake: good. note for postmortem: missing per-route dashboards caused delay in root-cause isolation. ops had to resort to traces. we spent ~6 minutes figuring out which prefix was affected.

product-ops: any customer impact? we have a few monitoring alerts from our enterprise customers. they reported occasional 500s for some endpoints.

maria: quick assessment: canary affected ~10% of traffic, of which ~80% used the prefix change, so roughly 8% of requests experienced elevated latency and ~0.6% experienced 5xx. duration ~23 minutes (start->kill), with most errors in first 10 minutes.

jake: logging this in the incident ticket: INC-2026-042. impact_level=minor, customers_impacted=some enterprise endpoints, recommended action: restore per-route dashboards, add canary guard in observability alerts, improve canary auto-kill threshold.

sasha: i'll pick this up for a follow-up: restore dashboards + add a dashboard tile that slices p95 by route prefix. will pair with observability team.

maria: also propose adding an automatic canary kill when a combination of p95+error rate triggers within 5m for canary cohort. Redwood Optimize already suggests batching/quant profiles — we can extend to routing checks.

deploy-bot: rollback complete. rollout rl_20260315_01 -> state=rolled_back.

jake: thanks all. handing off to sasha for the postmortem/next steps — i'm going offline for the oncall rotation.

sasha: taking over. i'll open the postmortem doc and tag owners. rough TL;DR I'll include observability gap and proposed fixes.

product-ops: flagged customers notified via status page and targeted emails. thanks for quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
